question: What main sign tells you a pregnant woman with pre-eclampsia has developed eclampsia?

options.A: A sudden spike in maternal body temperature
options.B: Severe vaginal bleeding resembling a placental abruption
options.C: The onset of generalized tonic-clonic seizures
options.D: The complete cessation of fetal heart activity

explanation: Eclampsia is diagnosed when a patient with pre-eclampsia experiences generalized seizures that do not have another neurological cause. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T1#BMP226_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why are changes in vision and bad headaches serious warning signs in a pre-eclamptic patient?

options.A: They indicate severe cerebral vasospasm and impending eclamptic seizures
options.B: They are harmless side effects of routine iron supplementation
options.C: They confirm that the amniotic sac has ruptured prematurely
options.D: They show that the liver is failing to process normal blood proteins

explanation: Headaches and vision changes happen when blood vessels in the brain spasm, signaling that a seizure might be coming. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T1#BMP226_U1_T1_h1)

question: What is the main reason for putting a seizing eclamptic patient on her side?

options.A: To prevent aspiration of vomit and maintain a clear airway
options.B: To completely stop the seizure activity without using drugs
options.C: To speed up the natural descent of the baby's head
options.D: To make it easier to start an intravenous line in the foot

explanation: The side-lying position uses gravity to keep saliva and vomit away from the windpipe, protecting the patient's breathing. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T1#BMP226_U1_T1_h2)

question: What is the first thing a midwife should do when a pregnant woman starts having a seizure in the ward?

options.A: Inject 20mls of sterile water directly into the umbilical cord
options.B: Turn her onto her side and call urgently for emergency assistance
options.C: Perform an immediate vaginal examination to check cervical dilation
options.D: Force a wooden spatula firmly between her teeth to stop tongue biting

explanation: Keeping the airway safe and getting help right away are the critical first steps during a seizure. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T1#BMP226_U1_T1_h2)

question: Which medication is used to reverse magnesium sulfate toxicity?
explanation: Calcium gluconate counteracts too much magnesium in the body and helps restore normal breathing. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T1#BMP226_U1_T1_h3)

question: Why must very high blood pressure in eclampsia be lowered gradually instead of all at once?

options.A: Sudden changes cause the mother's hair to fall out in large clumps
options.B: Normal blood pressure values deactivate the action of magnesium sulfate completely
options.C: Abrupt drops in blood pressure can severely reduce blood flow to the placenta and starve the fetus of oxygen
options.D: Rapid lowering triggers sudden blindness in the postpartum period

explanation: If blood pressure drops too fast, the placenta doesn't get enough blood, which can distress the baby. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T1#BMP226_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a standard first-choice drug for treating severe high blood pressure in pregnancy?
explanation: Furosemide is a water pill used for fluid in the lungs, not as the primary medicine to bring down dangerously high blood pressure in pregnancy. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T1#BMP226_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is the only treatment that completely cures eclampsia?

options.A: Strict bed rest in a dark room for seven days
options.B: Delivery of the fetus and placenta
options.C: Immediate closure of the cervical os with sutures

explanation: Eclampsia is caused by the placenta, so delivering it is the only way to stop the underlying condition. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T1#BMP226_U1_T1_h5)

question: When should delivery be planned after a patient has an eclamptic seizure?

options.A: Only after waiting exactly forty-eight hours to ensure lung maturity
options.B: Immediately during the active seizure phase without stopping to stabilize
options.C: Delayed until the patient reaches thirty-seven completed weeks
options.D: Promptly, as soon as maternal stabilization is successfully achieved

explanation: As soon as the mother is stable and safe, delivery should go ahead to protect both her and the baby. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T1#BMP226_U1_T1_h5)

question: How long should magnesium sulfate treatment usually continue after an eclamptic patient gives birth?

options.A: Until breast milk production is established
options.C: Until the mother is discharged home
options.D: For exactly 2 hours after clamping the cord

explanation: Magnesium sulfate is typically continued for 24 hours after birth to prevent seizures from returning. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T1#BMP226_U1_T1_h6)

question: Why is careful fluid monitoring so important in the postpartum care of a woman with eclampsia?

options.A: To ensure the baby receives enough breast milk every hour
options.B: To prevent fluid overload and subsequent pulmonary edema
options.C: To calculate the exact caloric intake needed for wound healing
options.D: To measure how fast the uterine involution process is occurring

explanation: Kidney changes in eclampsia make it easy for fluid to build up in the lungs if intravenous fluids are given too quickly. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T1#BMP226_U1_T1_h6)
